extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers conducting empirical/mixed-methods research on education markets (development economics, education policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules for conducting qualitative oral-history fieldwork and constructing merged administrative and survey datasets on schools, curricula, and electoral data in Indonesia (incl. coding rules, matching thresholds, and keyword-based classifications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative site selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Select field sites purposively using (i) the historical importance of Islamic schooling in the area, and (ii) madrasa and SD INPRES construction activities between 1973–80.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example sites used: Sijunjung (West Sumatra) and Lamongan & Gresik (East Java). Interviews were conducted in Fall 2021. Choose locations with documented variation in constructions (e.g., counts of MI/MTs/MA) to capture relevant local institutional contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent selection (snowball sampling and target roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use snowball sampling to identify respondents and target individuals who were directly involved at the time of establishment: SD INPRES teachers or principals when the school was first established; madrasa teachers or principals at time of establishment; community leaders (village heads, subdistrict heads) who were in office during the construction period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaching original founders may require intermediaries and multiple interactions. Report respondent age distribution (mean reported: 69 years) to document generational recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative sampling focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Purposively focus qualitative fieldwork on the Islamic sector's response to the SD INPRES program to reconstruct local histories and institutional contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document instances of competition, content/organizational responses, political pressures, funding mechanisms (e.g., waqf auctions) and capture anecdotes illustrating mechanisms (e.g., extra religious classes, local political influence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of household surveys for schooling measures (Susenas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure years and type of schooling using the annual National Socioeconomic Survey (Susenas) for selected years (2012, 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018). Merge with district-level INPRES intensity using respondent's birth district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify type (Islamic vs secular) and final level of certification; construct measure of Islamic schooling as the union of type and level indicators. Results should be robust when restricting to final-level certified or final-level attended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IFLS for Islamic attendance (descriptive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS) attendance data (1993, 1997, 2000, 2007, 2014) for descriptive analyses of Islamic school attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note geographic limitations of IFLS for econometric work; use IFLS primarily for descriptive tables (e.g., Table A.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative registries: madrasa data from MORA
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MORA registries for madrasa (primary, junior secondary, senior secondary) and informal diniyah, including village, district, and year of establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of missing establishment years (6% of madrasa, 22% of pesantren). Report and check that missingness is uncorrelated with key treatment variables (e.g., SD INPRES intensity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative registries: non-Islamic schools from Dapodik (MEC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the MEC Dapodik registry for formal non-MORA schools; includes village, district, and year of establishment for public and private schools (166,257 public; 52,888 private in source).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish privately-run Islamic-named schools within MEC by searching for specific name keywords (see separate classification rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of Islamic-named private schools (keyword rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify private schools likely to be Islamic-named by checking if the school name contains any of these terms: Islam, Darussalam, Darul, Muhammada, Salam, Sunna, Kuran, Jihad, Umma, Madrasa Halal, Imam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this binary keyword rule to separate private secular schools from private Islamic-named schools in Dapodik for robustness and subgroup analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Village-level panel construction and fuzzy matching threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a village-level panel using 2018 Podes as the master list and match school registries (Dapodik, MORA madrasa, diniyah, pesantren) via successive fuzzy merges using province code, district name, subdistrict name, and village name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a high matching score threshold (0.95) and require exact match on province code and district name. Report achieved match rates (e.g., 80% of villages in Dapodik, 84% in MORA madrasa, 62% diniyah, 66% pesantren) and document matching procedures and preprocessing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address preprocessing for diniyah and pesantren matches
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract village names from full address fields for diniyah and pesantren datasets after preprocessing the address string with extensive regular expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the regular-expression preprocessing steps and quality checks; lower match rates relative to registries with explicit village fields are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIAP curriculum data scraping and linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrape SIAP registry timetables (school–grade level weekly timetables) and link madrasa records to MORA registry using school IDs present in both sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIAP coverage was partial (~one-fifth of madrasa as of April 2020); acknowledge selective reporting and consider potential bias against core findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum string processing and subject categorization (regex rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parse SIAP strings to obtain subject names and durations for each period/day, then use regular expressions to classify each course into categories: (1) Islamic subjects, (2) Pancasila/Civic, (3) Bahasa Indonesia, (4) Arabic, (5) Math, (6) Natural Sciences, (7) Humanities, (8) Thematics (primary schools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the following keyword rules: Pancasila uses 'PPKn' or 'Pendidikan Pancasila dan Kewarganegaraan'; Bahasa uses 'Bahasa' or 'Indo'; Arabic uses keyword 'Arab' XOR keywords 'Fiq'/'Fik' (to separate Fiqh); Math uses 'Matematika'; Natural Sciences uses 'Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam', 'Fisika', 'Kimia', or 'Biologi'; Humanities uses 'Ilmu Pengetahuan Sosial', 'Ekonomi', 'Sejarah', 'Sosiologi', 'Wirausaha', 'Antropologi', or 'Geografi'; Thematics for primary schools uses exact beginning match 'Tematik'. Manually code Islamic subject titles and merge spelling variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematics subject mapping (policy-based rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map 'Tematik' subjects (introduced in the 2013 curriculum) to a set of underlying subjects: Indonesian language, PPKn, math, natural sciences, social sciences/humanities, arts & crafts, and physical education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect 'Tematik' exactly at beginning of subject string to classify primary-school thematic blocks; document compliance with Decree of the Ministry of Education and Culture number 67 year 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey/data-year selection for electoral and candidate data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use district-level vote shares from national legislative elections for specified years (1971, 1977, 1982, 1987, 1992, 1999, 2004, 2009) and use candidate universe data for 2019 scraped from KPU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying candidate motivations/platforms, search candidate statements for specified keywords (see campaign-motivation classification rubric). Document sources and scraping dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of campaign motivation/language proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify legislative candidates' campaign motivation and platform statements using keyword lists: Islamic-themed appeals keyed by 'umma', 'dawah', 'Muslim', 'Islam', 'sharia', 'jihad'; nation-building appeals keyed by 'Pancasila', 'Indonesia', 'NKRI', 'bangsa', 'bhinneka', 'satuan'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these linguistic proxies to construct binary indicators for campaign messaging; report dictionaries used and consider translation/orthographic variation during scraping.
